approved: user chat 2026-10-03: serverless CPU workers via a PRIVATE network volume (git archive + allow-listed checkpoints only, public base image), cpu5c preferred then cpu3c; serverless is the default backend for Tier-1 CPU jobs (pods = --backend pods). Per-world affinity (coordinator 2026-10-03, from the live pod runs): one world unit per worker, different worlds may run on different CPU models, so one endpoint rents cpu5c then cpu3c
price_source: coordinator-relayed console figures 2026-10-03 (not readable via the API; RunPod docs/pricing page list no serverless CPU rates); the run's billing guard aborts if /billing/endpoints exceeds the reserved rate
price_evidence: live billing read 2026-10-04 (GET /billing/endpoints, balance deltas in the run receipts): endpoint p1hxzbklf0a310 (kr-robust-d sls-resume, 10 x 2 vCPU cpu5c/cpu3c) billed $5.4116 for 32318 worker-seconds = $0.603 per 2-vCPU worker-hour, 7.2x the vCPU list price ($0.084, = GraphQL cpuFlavors.specifics.slsPrice) and 5.2x the ledger's reserved upper bound ($1.05); v8longh-b-r1 sls-run1b (10 x 2 vCPU) dropped the balance $3.12 for ~19800 worker-seconds (~$0.57/worker-hr, upper bound $0.65); e2e-sls (3 x 8 vCPU, ~175 worker-s of jobs) dropped it ~$0.02-0.06, about list. The in-run billing guard read $0 throughout (billing appears only after the endpoint is gone). Model: per worker max(vCPU x usd_per_vcpu_hr, usd_per_worker_hr_min); unverified at 16/32 vCPU, so every run also has the balance guard (balance_guard_seconds)
quota_note: RunPod live 2026-10-04: endpoint create fails (HTTP 500) with 'Max workers across all endpoints must not exceed your workers quota (10)'; the quota counts workersMax over ALL endpoints (not vCPUs: a CPU worker may have 32 vCPU). Before a run starts it sizes itself to the free workers or waits up to quota_wait_seconds (no run dir/ledger/watchdog yet), else exit 2; at create it re-checks for races
wall_note: pod-calibrated episode estimates x episode_time_factor (kr-robust-d sls-resume: planned 38.5 min, ran 59.0 = 1.53x; H5000 episodes on EPYC 7352 median 1.47x, max 3.12x the estimate; v8longh sls-run1b ran 0.66x of plan), and a plan's wall must be <= max_wall_fill x the run wall (a one-wave batch lasts as long as its slowest episode)
batch_note: a job carries whole world units (--units-per-job, default auto: filled to one wave of <= vCPU/2 episodes, the fewest jobs; a fixed K may run several waves and spreads over the workers); the records come back inside the /run result (RunPod caps it at 10 MB): <= max_job_output_mb over max(record_bytes_est, largest record seen) x 1.3
